prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the conception and demonstration of heterobifunctional degraders that induce targeted protein degradation

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration. Both parts turn a biological process into a defined chemical reaction and give biologists a general tool, and both have now been reproduced independently. Base editing is deaminase chemistry on one nucleobase, delivered by a programmable scaffold, with many independent laboratories and early clinical use. Induced-proximity degradation recasts drug action as event-driven chemistry: a small molecule forces a ubiquitin ligase onto a target, and ternary-complex formation and degradation kinetics can be measured. The first-round exchange did not weaken either case. B054 is the ballot most often named across the files, and B069 is a preference or alternative for six members, always with Liu as the central name. The pairing therefore draws on the broadest cross-member support rather than on my own ranking. The three-person cap works with Liu alone and Crews and Deshaies, and each attribution follows a conceptual originator rather than later developers.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is the one raised by Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Zou: base editing follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, and the deamination chemistry itself is classical, so the new element is protein engineering of the deaminase-Cas fusion and the evolved adenine deaminase. Long-term safety (bystander edits, RNA off-target deamination) is short. For degraders no heterobifunctional drug is approved, and Crews and Deshaies leave out Handa and Ito (cereblon), Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligands) and Sakamoto. Liu alone omits Komor and Gaudelli, and the Kondo and Nishida priority question for cytidine deamination is only partly answered by calling it a parallel publication. Two chemical-biology themes in one prize with only a loose link may also read as a weak unit, and no configuration yet has five supporters.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes a single-part degrader prize to Crews, Deshaies and Handa, covering both the heterobifunctional concept and the cereblon glue mechanism.
responses.response: I take your point that the glue mechanism is a distinct chemical finding, because identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target explained an old drug action and is measured in structures and kinetics. I still hold that the heterobifunctional concept is the separable, designable principle: a chemist can build a degrader for a chosen target, whereas glue activity was found retrospectively. If the committee prefers a single-part degrader prize, I would accept Crews, Deshaies and Handa and drop base editing. If it wants two parts, the cap forces Crews and Deshaies, and I would rather state openly that cereblon is omitted than blur the citation. Your note that no PROTAC is approved is fair; the concept rests on structure and kinetics, which are reproduced widely, not on approval.

responses.point: Somfai pairs C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) with base editing (Liu), and questions how much of base editing is new chemistry.
responses.response: I agree that deamination is classical and that the inventive step is engineering the deaminase-nickase fusion and evolving the adenine deaminase. My criterion is whether a biological process becomes a defined, controllable chemical reaction, and base editing meets it: the product is a specified single-base change that can be verified by sequencing. I also agree with your Liu-alone attribution. I am less persuaded that C-N coupling is untested, since only you ranked it in the openings and it overlaps the 2010 cross-coupling prize. A pairing with degraders gives a more coherent theme of chemical control of the genome and the proteome than two unrelated methods, and it asks the committee to test only one new combination.

responses.point: Aili prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles for Cullis, Anderson and Langer, and supports Liu alone for base editing.
responses.response: Your argument that the 2023 Medicine prize covered the cargo and not the carrier chemistry is sound, and the pKa-tuned lipid principle is clear and confirmed at a scale no other candidate reaches. My difficulty is still the credit. Hope, MacLachlan and Madden made decisive Vancouver contributions, and much of the optimisation was industrial, so I cannot name three people I could defend against the others. I keep B036 as my first alternative and would move to it if the committee agrees on a separable decisive step and its owner. I welcome your support for Liu alone and your reasoning that a prize honors the conceptual driver.

responses.point: Zou prefers halide perovskites for Miyasaka, Snaith and Park, and asks what a base-editing citation excludes if Kondo and Nishida are left out.
responses.response: Your question is fair. A Liu-only citation worded as base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single bases without double-strand cleavage, covers both the cytosine and the adenine editor, and it excludes the first Target-AID report of cytidine deamination by Kondo and Nishida, which appeared within weeks of Komor and Liu. I cannot settle that priority from the files, and I would want the expert report to compare dates and data. I accept that it is a real cost and I do not hide it. On perovskites, the replication and efficiency record are not in doubt, and I would move B017 to an alternative on my ballot because the absorber principle is demonstrated; the open stability question matters less for a citation about the absorber.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that base editing timing is not simply ripe because of the 2020 CRISPR prize and thin safety data, and that Kondo and Nishida deserve a hearing.
responses.response: I accept that the committee needs to be able to say what base editing adds beyond programmable cleavage. My answer is that it replaces a double-strand break and cellular repair with a direct chemical conversion of one base, which changes both the mechanism and the outcome distribution, and this is measured, not assumed. The safety record is short, and I list it openly, but the efficiency, product purity and reproduction across laboratories are established. I agree with you that the Target-AID priority question has to be addressed in the citation process and not set aside.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts two separate chemical-biology achievements in one prize or prefers a single-part prize.
Whether Crews and Deshaies without Handa, Ito and Ciulli is a fair credit, and whether the expert report treats the heterobifunctional concept and the cereblon glue as one achievement.
Whether base editing is judged sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether the Kondo and Nishida priority changes the credited names.
Whether any configuration can reach five votes given the spread across seven ballots.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is adjacent to nucleic-acid chemistry but I have no collaboration, institutional or funding tie to any shortlisted candidate, including those in the ubiquitin-ligase field. This is unchanged from round 1.
